turns.content: Hey. Sorry for the late message, I know it's almost midnight. I've been sitting here trying to draft a text to Tariq for about an hour now, and I keep deleting it. It's been nine months since he lost his job at that branding firm. He moved back into his parents' basement, which—fine, I get it, the economy is brutal. But he's stopped replying on Discord altogether, and last week I dropped off some nice markers and a sketchbook—nothing pushy, just something I thought might help—and he snapped at me. Told me to stop trying to "fix" him. I'm exhausted, honestly. I've been reading those relationship forums late at night, the ones about stonewalling and weaponized apathy, and I can't shake this bitter thought that maybe he's doing this on purpose. Like, punishing me for still having my life together. I know that sounds paranoid. Board game night is this Saturday—our old group. I want to invite him, just a casual one-line thing, no pressure. But I also don't know if I'm being an idiot for still reaching out. Can you help me draft something that doesn't sound desperate or accusatory?

You’re not an idiot for still caring. You’re also not crazy for being wiped after nine months of silence, a snapped-at sketchbook, and Discord going dead. That’s a lot to sit with at midnight.

Those forum posts make everything sound like a strategy. Sometimes it *is* someone shutting a door on purpose. A lot of the time, after a job loss and moving back home, it looks more like shame and freeze — he can’t match your life, so he disappears, then bristles when a gift feels like a progress report. Your bitter thought still makes sense as a feeling. It just doesn’t have to be the whole story, and you don’t have to solve that from a text.

A Saturday invite is different from “fixing him,” as long as you can send it and genuinely be okay with no reply. If you can’t, skip it this week. That’s allowed.

Something like this stays one line, casual, and easy to ignore:

**hey — board games saturday if you feel like it. no pressure either way**

That’s it. Don’t mention the markers, Discord, or that you miss him. If he doesn’t answer, don’t follow up about this one. You already showed up; the ball can sit on his side.

I appreciate the draft. It's clean. But I keep circling back to that bitter thought—the forums call it 'stonewalling'—and I need to ask you plainly: do you think he's punishing me on purpose, or is that just my exhaustion talking?

I can’t know what’s in his head. From what you’ve described, I would not treat “he’s punishing you on purpose” as the best read.

Nine months after a job loss, basement, Discord gone quiet, then snapping at a sketchbook, tracks more with shame and freeze than with a plan to hurt you. People in that spot often can’t stand being seen, so they vanish, then flinch at anything that feels like “get better.” The goal is usually to stop feeling small, not to dock you points for having a life.

Forums love a villain. Stonewalling *can* be a tactic. This looks sloppier than that: collapse, then a raw “stop fixing me,” not a campaign.

Your bitter thought still makes sense. Exhaustion plus silence will write a story, and resentment on his side can sit inside depression without it being a strategy. You don’t need a verdict to act on what’s already true: he’s not meeting you, and you’re allowed to be tired of carrying the outreach.

"Collapse, then a raw 'stop fixing me.' That's a good way to put it. I can feel the difference between that and a campaign."

So if I send that text and he ignores it, I'm okay with that. I've already decided I am. But there's a part of me that wants to put a deadline on this—like, if he skips Saturday, I'm done. Is that fair? Or am I just trying to preempt the hurt by making it my choice?

Wanting a limit is fair. Turning Saturday into a secret pass/fail is not quite the same thing.

He doesn’t know the stakes. If he’s in that freeze, skipping game night is the default, not a verdict on you. So “if he isn’t there, I’m done” is less a boundary and more a way to get the ending over with on your terms. That’s a very human move. It just doesn’t actually spare you the hurt — it just lets you call it a decision instead of a rejection.

A cleaner version of the same need:

You’re allowed to be done *chasing*. You’re allowed to send the one-line invite and then stop. You’re allowed to say, privately, “this is the last unprompted reach-out for a while.” That’s about your energy, not his attendance.

What I’d skip is the death-penalty clause. One no-show after nine months of collapse isn’t enough information to close the whole book. If you need distance, take the distance because you’re exhausted, not because he failed a test he never sat.

Send it if you still want him there. Then let Saturday be Saturday — not the trial.

That's a fair distinction. "Death-penalty clause" is an apt phrase. Saying "I'm done if he skips" does feel like I'm setting a trap for him, not a boundary for me.

Okay. I'll send the invite. No pass/fail on Saturday. Just the one line, and then I stop chasing for a while. That's the honest version, I think.

Yeah. That’s the honest version.

One line, no trap, no chasing after. Saturday can just be a night with the group — not a referendum.

If it sits weird after you send it, that’s allowed too. You don’t have to narrate it to him. You’ve already done the part that was yours.

I sent it. "board games saturday if you feel like it." No follow-up, no explanation. Felt clean.

Now I'm just sitting here wondering if that was the last thing I ever say to him as a friend.

That thought showing up right after you hit send is pretty normal. You finally put the chasing down, and your brain fills the quiet with a funeral.

It might be the last unprompted thing you say for a while. That’s different from “the last thing you’ll ever say as a friend.” You don’t actually know that yet, and you don’t have to decide it tonight.

You sent something kind and small. That’s a decent last line *if* it has to be one — and a decent open door if it isn’t. Either way, you don’t have to sit here rehearsing the ending. You already did the hard part.
